newsitem.title: UK: New Mideast-W.Africa airfreight link set for March.
newsitem.headline: New Mideast-W.Africa airfreight link set for March.

text.p: A new palletised airfreight connection between the Middle East and West Africa will be offered from next month following the signing of an interline agreement by Air Gabon and DAS Air, said UK cargo agent for both carriers, ANA Aviation Services.
ANA director Gil Harding told Reuters the new air cargo link will result from the start-up on March 19 of a new twice-weekly Libreville-Nairobi Boeing 767-200 passenger service by Air Gabon.
He said that one of the flights will call at Luanda in Angola on the outbound leg while the second will include a stopover at that city on the return sector.

"The plan is for cargo generated in the Middle East to be flown on DAS Air's twice-weekly freighter flights from Dubai to Nairobi, where it will then be transferred on to the new Air Gabon services to West Africa," he said.
DAS Air currently operates twice-weekly Dubai-Nairobi all-cargo flights, one with a 65-tonne capacity McDonnell Douglas DC-10F and the other with a Boeing 707F capable of carrying 40 tonnes.
From September, a second DC-10 freighter being purchased by Ugandan carrier DAS Air will replace the 707F on the route, increasing the weekly capacity offered to 130 tonnes.
Air Gabon's 767-200 can carry 10 tonnes of palletised cargo.
"We expect to attract quite a lot of consumer goods, textiles and general cargo out of the Middle East bound for West Africa," noted Harding.
He added that apart from Angola, destinations for these shipments will also include Lagos, Abidjan, and Dakar, all served by Air Gabon.
"From West Africa to the Middle East, we anticipate attracting a limited amount of comercial traffic, along with produce and flowers," he said.
